L30: ### What is Futures Trading?
L31: 
L32: cite39†Futures trading lets traders participate in market movements and potentially profit by going long or short on a futures contract. On Binance Futures, you may also use different leverage levels to reduce risk or potentially amplify profits in volatile markets.
L33: ### What are long and short in futures trading?
L34: 
L35: In spot trading, traders can only profit when the value of an asset increases. Futures trading, however, allows traders to potentially profit in both directions–whether the value of an asset rises or falls–by taking long or short positions on a futures contract.
L36:   * By going long, a trader buys a futures contract with the expectation that its value will increase in the future.
L37:   * Conversely, if a trader anticipates that the contract price will decrease in the future, they can sell a futures contract to go short.
L38: 
L39: For example, you anticipate that the BTC price is going to rise. You may go long to buy a BTCUSDT contract:
L40: 
L41: Contract Size  | Entry Price  | Exit Price  | Profit and Loss (PNL)
L42: 1 BTC  | 5,000 USD  | 5,500 USD  | 500 USD
L43: If you anticipate that the BTC price will fall, you may go short to sell a BTCUSDT contract:
L44: 
L45: Contract Size  | Entry Price  | Exit Price  | Profit and Loss (PNL)
L46: 1 BTC  | 5,000 USD  | 4,500 USD  | 500 USD
L47: ### How to trade on Binance Futures?
L48: 
L49: 1. Log in to your Binance account and go to the cite40†USDⓈ-M or cite41†COIN-M Futures trading page. If you don’t have a Futures account yet, please refer to "cite42†How to Open a Binance Futures Account? ".
L50: 
L51: 2. Transfer USDT or USDC to your USDⓈ-M Futures Account, or other coins (e.g., BTC) to your COIN-M Futures Account, as margin.
L52: 
L53: 3. Choose a symbol to trade and select a preferred leverage.
L54: 4. Choose an order type and customize the order details. Click [Buy/Long] or [Sell/Short] to place your order.
L55: ### How to calculate unrealized PNL and ROI%?
L56: #### USDⓈ-M Futures
L57: 
L58: Using Mark Price as the price basis:
L59: 
L60:   * Unrealized PNL = Contract Size * Absolute value of the position * Order Direction * (Mark Price - Entry Price)
L61:   * ROI% = Unrealized PNL in USDT or USDC / Entry Margin = ( (Mark Price - Entry Price) * Order Direction * Size) / (Contract Size * Mark Price* IMR)
L62:     * IMR = 1 / Leverage
L63: 
L64: Using Last Price as the price basis:
L65:   * Unrealized PNL = Contract Size * Absolute value of the position * Order Direction * (Last Price - Entry Price)
L66:   * ROI% = Unrealized PNL in USDT or USDC / Entry Margin = ( (Last Price - Entry Price) * Order Direction * Size) / (Contract Size * Mark Price* IMR)
L67:     * Order Direction:
L68:       * 1 for long orders
L69:       * -1 for short orders
L70: 
L71: The ROI% calculation has been updated to provide a more accurate reflection of your trading performance by including all related fees.
L72: ROI = (RealizedPNL + commissionFeeTotal + fundingFee + insuranceClearFee) / (entryPrice*openedVolum/leverage)
L73: 
L74: This means that the ROI now accounts for:
L75: 
L76:   * Realized Profit and Loss (realizedPNL)
L77:   * Total Commission Fees (commissionFeeTotal)
L78:   * Funding Fees (fundingFee)
L79:   * Insurance Clearing Fees (insuranceClearFee)
L80: 
L81: By including these fees, the ROI% gives you a clearer picture of your net returns on each position.
L82: #### COIN-M Futures
L83: 
L84: Using Mark Price as the price basis:
L85: 
L86:   * Unrealized PNL = Contract Size * Contract Multiplier * Absolute value of Position * Order Direction * (1 / Entry Price - 1 / Mark Price)
L87:   * ROI% = Unrealized PNL * Mark Price / abs(Size) * Contract Multiplier * IMR
L88: 
L89: Using Last Price as the price basis:
L90:   * Unrealized PNL = Contract Size * Contract Multiplier * Absolute value of Position * Order Direction * (1 / Entry Price - 1 / Last Price)
L91:   * ROI% = Unrealized PNL * Mark Price / abs(Size) * Contract Multiplier* IMR
